transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
My sleep has been all over the place lately. Some nights I’m up late planning and working on music, and other nights I can’t sleep at all or I end up sleeping half the day.
During those nights when you are up late working on music, do you feel an unusually high amount of energy or a decreased need for sleep compared to your normal baseline?

Yeah, during those bursts I feel a huge surge of restless energy and only need about three or four hours of sleep. I'll stay up until 4 AM tweaking mixes and wake up buzzing with ideas, feeling totally fine like sleep is just an inconvenience getting in my way.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting at least a week where you felt this energized, impulsive, or unusually talkative, resulting in significant problems at work or in your relationships?

Yes, I’ve been cycling through these high-energy, restless spurts on and off since my early twenties, usually lasting for several days or a week at a time. They definitely cause major problems, because I end up snapping at my wife and talking over her, and I've blown past important work deadlines and let our bills pile up.

During these high-energy episodes, have you ever required hospitalization, or did you experience any features like losing touch with reality, such as hearing voices or holding beliefs that others found clearly impossible?

No, I've never been hospitalized during those high-energy times, and I've never experienced anything like hearing voices or losing touch with reality. Even when my mind is racing with all those ideas, I still know what's real and what isn't.

To be absolutely sure, have you ever experienced any moments during these high-energy periods where you felt you possessed special powers, had a mission of great importance that others didn't understand, or felt like your thoughts were being broadcast to others?

No, I've never felt like I had literal superpowers, a grand mission, or that my thoughts were being broadcast. The closest I get is feeling like I have this "special grind mode" where I convince myself I can build an app or launch a channel and fix all our money problems overnight. But I know it’s not an actual superpower, just me getting overly confident.

During these high-energy episodes that last for a week, does the intensity of your symptoms cause a marked impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or are they manageable enough that you can still carry out your daily responsibilities?

While I'm in them, I feel totally fine and convinced I can handle everything, but they aren't actually manageable. I get so scattered starting multiple projects and jumping from task to task without finishing anything. This disorganization, along with the crashes that follow, makes me blow past deadlines and lose track of our bills.

When you are in these high-energy states, is the impairment in your functioning severe enough that you are unable to work or maintain your social relationships for the duration of the episode, or are you still able to function at a basic level?

During those high phases, I actually feel like I'm functioning at a super-high level—I'm constantly busy messaging people, planning projects, and doing basic tasks, so I'm not completely incapacitated. But it still causes real problems because I start a million things without finishing them, snap at my wife over budget questions, and ultimately wind up blowing past deadlines anyway.

During these high-energy episodes, have you ever experienced a period lasting at least four consecutive days where your mood and activity levels were clearly different from your usual self, but you were still able to function in your daily life without them being severe enough to cause a complete disruption in your work or social life?

Yes, those high-energy phases usually last at least four days to a week, and my mood is definitely different from my normal self during them. I'm still able to get out of bed and work on projects during those up times, which is completely different from my low periods where I shut down entirely and can't function at all.

During these high-energy episodes, have you ever had a period where your symptoms were so severe that you were unable to work or maintain your social relationships at all, necessitating professional intervention or hospitalization?

No, I've never been hospitalized or had high phases so severe that they completely incapacitated me. While they do cause a lot of chaos with unfinished projects, this clinic visit is actually my very first time seeking professional psychiatric help. I only came in now because the constant cycling and my recent deep lows are completely ruining our finances and my job search.

To clarify the degree of impairment, during these high-energy episodes, would you say your functioning is unequivocally different from your usual self, but still allows you to maintain your job and social responsibilities without the level of disruption that would typically require hospitalization?

Yes, my behavior is definitely very different from my normal self during those times—my wife notices it immediately because I'm so amped up, talking a mile a minute, and barely sleeping. While I've never needed hospital care and can still technically function day-to-day, it still causes real problems because I take on way too much, never finish projects, and constantly snap at my wife.

During these high-energy episodes, have you ever experienced a distinct period lasting at least one full week where the symptoms were so severe that you were completely unable to function at your job or in your social life, even if you weren't hospitalized?

I don't think my high-energy periods have ever lasted a full week where I was completely unable to function. Even when they get pretty chaotic, I can still get things done, so I'm not sure they've ever been that severe for that long.
